title: The "White Rock" of Shiroishi City
description: Shiroishi City in southern Miyagi is renowned for its reconstructed castle, samurai history, special 'umen' noodles, and the enchanting Zao Fox Village. While exploring attractions and savoring local cuisine are popular activities, researching the origins of the place names offers valuable insights into the history and thoughts of past pioneers. Shiroishi (白石) translates to 'White Rock,' and this rock still exists in a small chained-off enclosure. Located just a 5-minute walk from City Hall or a 10-minute walk from Shiroishi Castle, the rock is accompanied by a pine tree and a historical marker. The 'white' rock is actually ash gray, having weathered the elements for centuries. Standing at 0.47 meters tall and 1.05 meters in diameter, it is considered a resting place for a matchmaking deity. The city is linked to a larger white rock in Neno-Shiroishi, located about 55km away, where prayers for good marriages are said to be fulfilled.

title: Sendai's Flagship Street Food: Hyotan
description: Without a doubt, one of Sendai's must-try street foods is 'hyotan-age'. This delightful snack consists of deep-fried fish balls skewered on a stick, offering a crispy exterior and a soft interior. Served with a swirl of optional ketchup, it resembles an American corndog in texture. You can find hyotan-age at Sendai Station near the tourism information center or at the original Abe Kamaboko shop at the end of the CLIS Road shopping arcade. For just ¥250, this portable snack is perfect for a break during shopping. And if you find the word 'あたり' on your stick, you are a 'winner'!

Nakiryu Ramen
description: Nakiryu Ramen (創作麺工房 鳴龍) is a Michelin-starred ramen restaurant located in Tokyo's Otsuka district. Opened in 2012, it quickly became one of Tokyo's best ramen shops, earning its Michelin star in 2017. Nakiryu offers a variety of ramen options, including shoyu, shio, and their signature tantanmen, known for its creamy, spicy broth and handmade ultra-thin noodles. The basic tantanmen starts at ¥900, with spicier and sourer variations available. Open from 11 am to 3:30 pm, closed on Tuesdays, Nakiryu is just a 6-minute walk from Otsuka Station. Don't miss the chance to experience this culinary gem!

title: Youmeiji Temple, Tsuwano
description: Youmeiji Temple (永明寺) is a thatch-roofed temple located 15 minutes from Tsuwano Station and 10 minutes from the old town center. I visited in early summer and felt a refreshing breeze from the tall trees and thick forest after climbing the stairs to the temple. The entrance features a tall gate that once marked the boundary between the merchant town and samurai residences. The temple is quiet, allowing weary travelers to relax. Behind the temple is a small but beautiful garden. Built in 1420 by the Yoshimi clan, it served as the family temple for domain lords until the Meiji Restoration. The graveyard in front includes the resting place of Ogai Mori, a prominent Meiji period writer. A unique hollow fish sculpture serves as a silent alarm for the priests, adding to the temple's serene atmosphere. This is a place worth visiting.

description: Gyorai Ramen (本枯中華そば 魚雷) is a unique ramen shop located in Bunkyo, Tokyo, that opened in 2010. Its standout feature is the use of coffee siphons for soup preparation, which maximizes the smoky flavor from dried bonito. The ramen is served in a 'deconstructed' style, allowing customers to choose their toppings and customize their dish. The basic ramen starts at ¥730, with options for deluxe (¥930) and grilled (¥1,030) versions, each offering a variety of toppings. The soup is made from Aomori jidori chicken, Akaniwatori chicken from Kagoshima, and pork, blended with kombu and various fish flavors. With its innovative cooking method and high-quality ingredients, Gyorai Ramen is a must-visit for ramen lovers.

title: Sunny Hills at Minami
description: Located in the glitzy neighborhood of Omotesando, Sunny Hills (微熱山丘) is a pineapple cake shop housed in a stunning wooden structure designed by renowned architect Kengo Kuma, completed in 2013. This architectural marvel utilizes over 5000 meters of timber and traditional woodcrafting techniques without any nails. Visitors can freely explore the three-story building and enjoy a complimentary pineapple cake, 'Sunny Delights,' along with tea on the second floor, embracing Taiwanese hospitality. It's a perfect spot to unwind away from the bustling Tokyo coffee shops, offering a unique experience in a serene atmosphere.

title: The 1300th Anniversary of Koma
description: In 2016, Koma in Hidaka City, Saitama, celebrates its 1300th anniversary. The name Koma (高麗) is also associated with Goguryeo, an ancient kingdom. The Nihon Shoki records the arrival of Jakko, an envoy from Goguryeo, in Japan. In 716 A.D., Jakko gathered 1,799 Goguryeo refugees and settled them in the Musashino Plain. After his death, the Koma Shrine was built in his memory. Exciting events are planned for May 21-22, 2016, including a memorial concert and the Rainbow Parade, where participants will wear colorful Korean-style clothing, commemorating the arrival of the refugees. A giant pot of Koma Nabe will be served at the end of the parade.

title: Matsumoto Kiyoshi
description: Japan is renowned not only for its high-tech gadgets but also for its excellent cosmetic brands and quality medicines. In Tokyo, you can find numerous drugstores, with Matsumoto Kiyoshi being the largest chain. It offers a wide range of both Japanese and international cosmetics and medicines, making it a perfect shopping destination for beauty-conscious customers. Brands like Shiseido, Kose, and Maybelline are available, along with testers for customers to try before they buy. Additionally, Matsumoto Kiyoshi stocks various products, including food, pet supplies, and toiletries. The store is easily recognizable by its vibrant blue and yellow signage, featuring the kanji for 'medicine' (薬) prominently displayed. Shopping at Matsumoto Kiyoshi promises to be a delightful experience.

description: Kameki Sushi (亀喜寿司) is celebrated as one of Japan's top sushi restaurants, frequented by the elite when they travel north of Tokyo. It is featured on the local government's 'Sushi Road' for serving fresh fish from the Shiogama fish markets. With over 80 years of history, Kameki Sushi has grown alongside the success of Shiogama's fishing industry. The menu offers a wide variety of options, including set menus (from ¥5,200), chirashi, nigiri, maki, and sashimi. A highlight is the egg cake with surimi (¥300) from their unique dessert menu. Seasonal specialties abound, showcasing the rich marine life off the East Japan coastline. A visit to Kameki Sushi is a must for sushi enthusiasts traveling through Miyagi Prefecture.

After the Great Kanto Earthquake, it developed as a substitute for Tokyo's confectionery wholesalers, and now features over 20 shops where visitors can enjoy nostalgic flavors. The unique vibrancy of the artisans and the sweet aromas create a delightful atmosphere for strolling and snacking. The close-knit community adds warmth to the experience. Every April, the Kashiya Yokocho Festival is held, showcasing traditional performances. Kawagoe City is also set to host the golf venue for the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, with efforts to accommodate foreign tourists.

In addition to snacks, these shops offer commemorative stamps and old bills, making each visit a delightful experience. Collecting these stamps provides a unique glimpse into Japanese art and culture, making Dagashi-ya a must-visit for anyone interested in the charm of childhood and Japanese heritage.

description: While searching for Niku Zushi in Sangenjaya, we stumbled upon Ro to Matagi (炉とマタギ) next door. This unique restaurant specializes in deer meat and is housed in a renovated Showa-era building. The lively izakaya-style first floor contrasts with the quiet, hunting lodge vibe of the second floor. The menu features Ezo deer, Inobuta (a hybrid of wild boar and pig), and Bobo Yasai with Matagi Cauda dip. The deer meat was tender and flavorful, while the Inobuta was equally delicious. A perfect spot for those seeking a new culinary adventure!

title: Yokohama’s Soji
description: The beautiful long corridor 'Hyak-ken-rou-ka' (百間廊下) stretches 152 meters, symbolizing the boundary between the sacred and the ordinary. At 4 AM, a young monk runs through the temple corridors, ringing a loud wake-up bell, marking the start of a new day. Fifteen minutes later, 160 monks begin their morning zazen on meditation platforms. Soji-ji, one of the two largest Zen temples of the Soto sect, was established after a fire destroyed its original buildings, leading to its reconstruction in Yokohama. Located just a 7-minute walk from JR Tsurumi station, this temple is uniquely close to the city. The temple grounds feature twelve large buildings and a cemetery, covering nearly 50,000 square meters. Visitors are welcome to explore the beautiful grounds and can also experience the interiors of the temple buildings.

title: Kawasaki Daishi: A Beautiful and Famous Temple in Kawasaki
description: Kawasaki Daishi (川崎大師) is one of the must-visit temples during your stay in Japan. With easy access and a vibrant local atmosphere, this temple is grand and beautiful. It attracts a mix of locals, tourists, and special visitors. Each year, nearly 3 million people visit for Hatsumode on New Year's Eve to offer their prayers. The temple also hosts monthly fairs, Noh theater performances, and a charming wind chime market in July, providing a great opportunity to experience traditional culture. Kawasaki Daishi is known as a center for spreading the teachings of Kobo Daishi. Don't miss the tea ceremony event in April if you're interested in traditional Japanese culture.

title: Vintage Shopping in Hiroshima
description: Hiroshima city center is a haven for shoppers, especially on Hondori, the main shopping arcade. While many stores focus on current fashion trends, vintage lovers will find a special charm in timeless pieces. Initially, I thought Hiroshima lacked vintage shops until I discovered four fantastic stores on the fifth floor of Sunmall: Union Rag, Rag Moo, Yellow, and 3びきの子ねこ (Kitten Miki). These shops offer high-quality vintage clothing and accessories from the 60s to the 90s at reasonable prices. Union Rag and Rag Moo boast the largest and most varied stock, including popular Doc Martens and Converse shoes. Embrace the vintage allure and enjoy creating unique outfits that stand out.

title: Kanazawa Hakkei’s Chiyomoto [Closed]
description: Chiyomoto (千代本) is an authentic Japanese restaurant that frequently appeared in Hiroshige's ukiyo-e woodblock prints around 1834. This restaurant has stood for almost 200 years in the heart of what was once a famous scenic spot—Kanazawa Hakkei. All rooms in Chiyomoto face the sea, and in the past, guests arrived by boat. The interior is purely Japanese, retaining the atmosphere of its glorious past. The dishes are beautifully presented, with fresh ingredients cooked to perfection. Chiyomoto offers a unique experience where history and stunning views come together.

title: Hinano Organic Buffet in Moriya [Closed]
description: Hinano (旬菜食健ひな野) is a buffet-style restaurant that focuses on healthy ingredients, starting in Sendai in 2007. With over 50 outlets nationwide, it offers locally sourced, organic dishes at affordable prices. For ¥1,575 at lunch and ¥2,100 at dinner, you can enjoy a variety of traditional Japanese dishes, including salads, soups, curries, tempura, and tofu. While predominantly vegetarian, there are also meat and fish options available, with seasonal menus that change regularly. Hinano is a great place to indulge in delicious and healthy cuisine, making it a must-visit.

title: 2021年度森の京都文化観光サポーターラジオ 第3回「丹波の漆かき」
description:
This is the broadcast audio of the radio program "Mori no Kyoto presents Shittoru? Traditional Culture in Fukuchiyama" on Kyoto FM Tanba. The Mori no Kyoto Cultural Tourism Supporters introduce intangible cultural assets in Fukuchiyama from the perspective of supporters once a month.

 The third episode is about "Tamba Urushi (lacquer)". Yaku no Town in Fukuchiyama City, Kyoto Prefecture, has been one of Japan's leading lacquer-producing areas since ancient times, where lacquer craftsmen are preserving and passing on this traditional industry.

 The first half of the program covers the basics of lacquer. Lacquer tapping was popular during the Edo period, and currently, 90% of the lacquer used is imported. We will introduce the amazing qualities of this precious domestic lacquer!

 In the second half, we welcome guest Kousuke Yamauchi, a lacquer craftsman and public relations officer of the NPO Tamba Urushi, to talk about his encounter with lacquer, the reasons for moving to Fukuchiyama, the challenges he faces, and the charm of lacquer. The supporters were also moved by Yamauchi's passionate feelings towards lacquer, which left a refreshing impression!

title: Hiroo Town Santa Land ／北海道の絶景景色 【BESTHOKKAIDO_VOL.123】
description: This time, we will introduce 'Santa Land' in Hiroo Town. Hiroo Town, located in Tokachi, Hokkaido, is the first SantaLand in Japan and the first outside Japan to be recognized by Oslo, Norway, the hometown of Santa Claus. We have formed a friendship and exchange partnership with Frogn City, the base of Santaland's activities, and are developing the town based on Santaland's basic philosophy of 'Love, Peace, Gratitude and Service.' The 'Santaland Tree Lighting Ceremony' is the earliest Christmas lighting ceremony in Japan, and the 'Santaland Illumination' with 150,000 lights can be enjoyed from November. Additionally, in 2020, a Christmas tree was planted as a symbol. This place is recommended for couples.

title: Superb view of Hokkaido／オホーツク海から望む網走
description: This time, we will introduce the Sea of Okhotsk as seen from Abashiri City. Facing the Sea of Okhotsk, Abashiri is an area surrounded by the sea and lakes, with Lake Notoro, the Abashiri Quasi-National Park, and Lake Abashiri, which is also known as a scenic spot. And above all, it is famous for its drift ice, and the sight of the sea of Okhotsk dyed in pure white every year by the drift ice that comes from Siberia never ceases to fascinate those who see it. As the word 'Okhotsk Blue' suggests, driving while admiring the clear sky and the scenery along the Sea of Okhotsk is also recommended.

title: Lake Saroma Observatory 4K／Hokkaido's Superb Scenery 【BESTHOKKAIDO_VOL.114】北海道の絶景景色
description: This time, we will introduce the 'Lake Saroma Observatory' in Saroma-cho, Okhotsk. Lake Saroma Observatory is the only place where you can see the whole of Lake Saroma, which is the third largest lake in Japan, and there are no high mountains around, so you can enjoy a magnificent panorama that can only be seen here. From the observatory, you can also see the sandbar, also known as the 'Ryugu Kaido' that separates the lake and the sea, and the Shiretoko mountain range in the distance on a clear day. The observatory has three telescopes, and you can see every corner of Lake Saroma, and the view is first-class.

description: This time, we will introduce 'Lake Poroto' in Shiraoi Town, Hokkaido. Lake Poroto is a lake with a circumference of about 4 km and an area of 33 ha. In a place rich in nature with moors and forests surrounding it, Poroto means 'big swamp' in the Ainu language. On the shore of the lake on the south side of the lake, there is the national center 'Upopoy', a symbolic space for ethnic symbiosis, which introduces the history of the Ainu, which reproduces the traditional Ainu settlement. In winter, you can enjoy smelt fishing with freezing on one side.

description: The 70km-long Shimanami Kaido in Japan is one of the world’s most beautiful and accessible bike routes, and is enjoyable at any time of the year. The CYCLING SHIMANAMI event, however, is a true festival of cycling. Around 7,000 riders come from all over Japan and around the world for the rare opportunity to ride the iconic route via the expressway, the awesome views, local hospitality and relaxed vibe. In 2022, CYCLING SHIMANAMI returned after a 4 year hiatus and was held under clear blue skies, in bright sunshine – perfect conditions for island hopping by bike. The islands look absolutely stunning and we hope that this short film will prompt you to start planning your own cycling adventure on the Shimanami Kaido and Yumeshima Kaido. We are looking forward to welcoming you to Shimanami!

description: This is the broadcast audio of the radio program 'Mori no Kyoto presents Do you know? Traditional Culture in Fukuchiyama' on Kyoto FM Tanba. Two years after the previous series 'Do you know? Traditional Culture in Fukuchiyama', this series features regular guest Cahal from Ireland, who lives in Fukuchiyama, and focuses on the intangible cultural assets and traditional culture of Fukuchiyama. In the third episode 'Tamba Urushi & Yaku no Ki to Urushi no Kan', the first half introduces the history of Japanese lacquer and what was used instead of lacquer overseas. In the second half, we welcomed Akiko Hiraoka, the director of 'Yaku no Ki to Urushi no Kan' located in Yaku no Town, Fukuchiyama City. The museum introduces Tamba lacquer and displays tools used for lacquer tapping, as well as offering experiences in lacquer application and kintsugi. We discussed what activities are conducted at the museum and the director's efforts in promoting Tamba lacquer.

Two years have passed since the previous series 'Do you know? Traditional Culture in Fukuchiyama', and this series features regular guest Cahill, who lives in Fukuchiyama and discusses the intangible cultural assets and traditional culture of Fukuchiyama. In the second episode 'Washi & Tango Futamata Paper Preservation Society', the first half introduces the history of paper and the differences between Western paper and Japanese paper. In the second half, we invited Yoshiko Ohmori, the daughter of Toshihiro Tanaka, the fifth generation of Tanaka Paper Industry, which is the only inheritor of Tango Washi, to talk about her motivation to become a washi craftsman, her current feelings, and the activities of the Tango Futamata Paper Preservation Society.

description: This is the broadcast audio of the radio program 'Mori no Kyoto presents Do you know? Traditional Culture in Fukuchiyama' on Kyoto FM Tanba. title: 【関東最大級・あじさいの森】今年も6月中旬から『あじさい祭り』を開催します！1200品種28,000株のあじさい園に行こう♪
description: Ajisai no Mori, located in Kitai-baraki City, Ibaraki Prefecture, is one of the largest hydrangea gardens in Kanto, boasting 1,200 varieties and 28,000 hydrangeas in full bloom. After exiting at Kitai-baraki IC on the Joban Expressway, it takes about 10 minutes by car towards Mizunuma Dam and Hanazono Valley to reach the site. Each year, from mid-June to late June, 320 varieties of Yamajisai and Ezoajisai are in full bloom, and from mid-June to mid-July, 600 varieties of Temari-type and Gaku-blooming hydrangeas reach their peak. The garden features 320 varieties of wild Yamajisai collected by the Japan Hydrangea Association, as well as about 150 original varieties cultivated by Japanese breeders, providing a stunning display of hydrangeas. Additionally, visitors can enjoy the rare foreign species Anabelle and Kashiwaba hydrangeas.

description:
The 'Hanazono Auto Campground' located in Kitaibaraki City, Ibaraki Prefecture.
Ibaraki Prefecture is famous for having about 160 campgrounds in the prefecture, making it one of the most diverse camping fields in the country.
Among them, this campground is popular as a riverside field.

*Please make sure to watch with subtitles ON*

The auto camping sites (about 70㎡) are equipped with AC power and private water supply, making them very beginner-friendly!
There is also a motorhome site (150㎡) that can accommodate large vehicles.
Inside the campground, there is a flowing river where families can enjoy water play, making it popular among family customers!

Additionally, since the 'Hanazono River' flows near the campground, you can enjoy camping while listening to the sound of the clear stream♪
At night, the sky is filled with shining stars, captivating the hearts of campers...

Around the campground, there are many attractions such as 'Hanazono Shrine', which attracts many tourists from all over the country for its blessings of children and safe childbirth, the beautiful 'Nanatsutaki' during fresh greenery and autumn foliage, trekking at 'Eizoushitsu' and 'Oshozan', scenic autumn views at 'Hanazono Valley', and fishing experiences and river fish lunches at 'Masubuchi Fish Garden', so there are plenty of fun activities for the second day of camping too!!

Please create wonderful memories at the Hanazono Auto Campground in Kitaibaraki City＊

title: 空から見たみちのく潮風トレイル～春・夏・秋～
description: This is a perspective you don’t get to see on foot: let us show you how lovely the Michinoku Coastal Trail is from the sky. We start with scenes of cherry blossoms in the spring, then the forest and sea along the meandering ria coastline, the glowing sunset reflecting from calm bay waters, and white waves crashing against the rocks. Enjoy the many faces of the ever changing ocean along the Michinoku Coastal Trail from a bird’s perspective.

title: みちのく潮風トレイル南部～春・夏・秋～／MCT Southern Part: Spring, Summer, Fall
description: See everyday moments for hikers following the Michinoku Coastal Trail, including natural scenery along the trail, conversations with local people and time spent with other hikers. This video also shows hiking on various islands characteristic of the southern part of the trail and the Soma Nomaoi Festival, an ancient horse festival. (Filmed in areas between Soma, Fukushima Prefecture and Ofunato, Iwate Prefecture)

title: Interviews of Locals | 地域の声を聞く
description: There are people who feed hikers delicious food, those who helped make the trail, who provide spots to rest, those who protect and preserve the trail each day, those who maintain mountain hiking courses, those who support local industry and those who ferry hikers from island to island. And let’s not forget the local people who come up and talk to hikers. There are so many trail angels along the Michinoku Coastal Trail!

title: Interviews of Hikers／ハイカーの声を聞く
description: “Journeys are about the people. The true pleasure of travel is in meeting people. That’s why long distance trails aren’t just hiking in the mountains. Long distance trails are about close connections with local areas, towns and people.” --Shin Hasegawa, MCT thru-hiker (2018) “When you interact with other human beings who have experienced such tragedy it really sticks with you and resonates with you on a personal level. Not just focusing on the sad side, but hearing the stories of hope and resilience, that people rebuilt their lives and have this huge smile. It’s really just a magical experience to have these interactions with people in Tohoku. It’s a really life-changing experience.” --Robin Lewis, MCT thru-hiker (2017)

title: 空から見たみちのく潮風トレイル～秋・冬～
description: See the impressive footage we can expect from drones: majestic scenes of coastline and river mouths, as well as seemingly endless stretches of seawall and tsunami monuments. A highly recommended video because it shows, in a condensed form, the variety of the over 1000 kilometer long Michinoku Coastal Trail running from Hachinohe in Aomori Prefecture to Soma in Fukushima Prefecture. Get a grasp of the massive scale of this landscape by watching for occasional appearances by miniature hikers.

title: MCT南部：秋と冬
description: See scenes from the southern part of the Michinoku Coastal Trail in fall and winter as we follow the progress of a single hiker. The southern part of this trail has many historical sites and tsunami monuments, and because it goes through rural landscapes and villages, you can more closely experience people’s daily lives.

title: Smooth Pudding and Light Chiffon Cake Specialty Store 'Niwa no Niwatori' Visited by Tourism Association Staff
description:
🍮 Do you like sweets? 🍮

The tourism association staff went to 'Niwa no Niwatori' in Kitahiroshima Town in search of sweets!!

'Niwa no Niwatori' is a specialty store for smooth pudding and light chiffon cake run by the Yokoyama couple.

As soon as you open the door, a sweet aroma wafts through. Your heart dances at the sight of the lined-up puddings and chiffon cakes.

Being a confectionery workshop of an egg shop, the sweets do not use any fragrances, so the taste of the eggs is prominent. They have won first place in the online pudding category!✨️

The staff's recommendation is 'Pudding Madonna', a richly smooth and rewarding sweet. The slightly bitter caramel is irresistible.

The adorable strawberry milk pudding is a limited-time offer, available until around May. The生チョコプリン, which harmonizes high cacao chocolate and eggs, is also a popular product.🍫

The chiffon cake is fluffy, like a cloud. There are plenty of varieties such as tea, chocolate, and cherry blossom, making it perfect for gifts. The meringue cookies and chiffon cake rusk are also exquisite.

Even during filming, laughter never ceased, creating a warm atmosphere that conveys the Yokoyama couple's personality in this short video.🌷

For a reward for yourself or a gift for a loved one, be sure to enjoy these 'heart-melting' delightful sweets.

[Niwa no Niwatori]

title: Mysterious 'Ice Waterfall Tour' ⛄⛄ #KitahiroshimaTown #KitahiroshimaCity
description:
Have you ever climbed a snowy mountain??⛄️

Limited season! The 'Ice Waterfall Monitoring Tour' planned by Mr. Kurata from the wild glamping and camping site 'Ryuzunomori' in Toyohira was attended by staff from the tourism association🧊!!

This is my second time climbing Mount Ryuto in mid-winter. We progress while stepping on the snow with a crunch.

To keep the climbing interesting, Mr. Kurata provides mountain trivia and quizzes🏔️.

Just as I was starting to get a bit out of breath, we arrived at the first highlight, 'Koma Falls'. If the timing is right, you can see the frozen waterfall🧊. On this day, the weather was a bit nice, so it was melting, but there were still icicles here and there, and the frozen grass and trees looked like jewels💎.

At the second spot, 'Kuro Falls', there were icicles that had melted and pierced into the ground!! It's about the same height as the staff member who is 167 cm tall... I felt the power of nature.

And the beauty of the snowy mountain bathed in sunlight!!
It was a quiet and mysterious space where only the chirping of birds and the sound of the wind could be heard.

After descending, we had lunch at the cafe 'Caf'e de la Richesses 六' near the trailhead🍽️.

I had Mr. Kurata's special spice keema curry and homemade marmalade tea, which warmed me up! Sharing our thoughts about the tour while warming up by the fireplace was a leisurely and luxurious time☺️.

It was a mysterious ice waterfall tour that allowed us to fully enjoy the winter scenery of Mount Ryuto, which is rarely seen✨.

🧊 This ice waterfall tour will also be held on ★2/8 (Sat) and ★2/11 (Tue)!!! If you're interested, please DM Ryuzunomori. (Since there is a possibility of the tour being held in the snow, beginners in climbing are requested to refrain from participating.) Search for 'Ryuzunomori'🔍

title: 【古民家】洗礼された宿でた特別な時間を過ごす。
description:
✨️The staff of the tourism association visited the one-house rental old folk house "hitaru Ishibashi-tei" in Oasa✨️ This is the long version!

As you go up to a slightly elevated area, the old folk house appears with a warm light.

Built 200 years ago. The residence of a swordsmith was renovated by "Fumu Co., Ltd."

Upon entering, a spacious area with a chic atmosphere based on black spreads out. Wow... it's beautiful.

The Ishibashi-tei, themed as a food guest house centered around the kitchen, allows you to enjoy seasonal ingredients that you procure yourself, or savor the exceptional dishes prepared by selected chefs.

The large round table that surrounds the blissful dining experience is actually a remade lid of a sake barrel from "Fukumitsu Sake Brewery" located in the same Oasa area 🍶✨️

To immerse guests in the "extraordinary," every detail of the furniture and interior has been carefully considered. (All electrical appliances are BALMUDA 😲)

I wanted to try this! There are also appliances I've always admired. The mirror with LED lights also raises my spirits 🪞

Enjoying the garden includes bonfires and BBQs. Even on cold days, the time spent gazing at the crackling fire brings peace to the heart. Without streetlights, once your eyes adjust to the pitch darkness, a starry sky appears. When was the last time I gazed at the stars...

When the sun rises, right in front of you is "Oasa Fuji," also known as Kanbiki Mountain. The chirping of birds in the majestic nature is the unique BGM of Ishibashi-tei ☺️

There are two bedrooms, and one room has futons. It's quite rare that it can accommodate up to 12 guests.

An "extraordinary" experience just an hour's drive from Hiroshima city.
Precious time with your loved ones.

Here at "hitaru Ishibashi-tei," there is a luxurious time that cannot be experienced in the city, where you can "eat," "sleep," and "immerse" yourself.

title: Autumn Cycling Tour in Kitahiroshima Town🍂🍂
description:
✨️ A staff member from the tourism association went to the autumn cycling tour at 'O.M.S. Oasa Mobility Station'✨️

O.M.S. is a place where cyclists and tourists can gather, transforming the former Oasa bus station.

It is a spot where not only bus users but also cyclists and visitors to Oasa can easily stop by.

Here, you can take part in tours using sports-type electric assist bicycles (E-BIKES) or rent bicycles, with parking and bike storage available, as well as maintenance and cycling course guidance.

The O.M.S. also accepts registrations for the Kakeiyama Hill Climb Challenge🔥

The autumn course that the tourism staff was guided through is only available at this time of year.

Although I was a bit out of breath from the久しぶりの運動, the refreshing view from Kakeiyama instantly revitalized me!!

The salt rice balls eaten at the top are simple yet the best🍙

After Kakeiyama, we headed to the ginkgo trees at Saikyoji Temple and the Hotokebara Amusement Park!
This video was taken on November 4th, but it seems that this weekend will be the most beautiful✨️

This tour is filled with the rich knowledge and flexible course development of guide Mr. Tagawa, and above all, his passionate desire to entertain every customer.

The tour can be arranged to suit each individual customer, allowing everyone to enjoy an original tour✨️

Along the way, he shares core information about the history and culture of the Oasa region, as well as trivia that only locals know, making it not only fun but also educational.

With Mr. Tagawa's charming and warm guidance, I didn't feel tired at all during the cycling☺️

Please come and meet the professional Mr. Tagawa from Oasa!!

title: ＼旬感！ 菊もみ！ 学生記者クラブ／
description: From November 1 to November 7, the 'Hirosaki Castle Chrysanthemum and Autumn Leaves Festival' is being held at Hirosaki Park. Students from Hirosaki University have become reporters for the festival (commonly known as 'Kiku-Momi') and have conducted undercover coverage! We will deliver the production scenes of flower art and how to enjoy the festival. Some of you may have already visited? Although it's a bit late, this time we will deliver the order of appreciation to enjoy flower art more deeply. The dragon that came from the east passes through the East Gate and enters the Hirosaki Castle Botanical Garden. After passing through the flower arch, the dragon sits in the San-no-Maru Garden with a white flower on its head. The flower water represents the dragon's footprints. The apple tree towering next to the dragon bears red fruits filled with wishes. The flower water heading towards the Otemon from the apple tree overflows with apple leaves that have fallen from the tree, and a large apple is bearing fruit on the Otemon side of the San-no-Maru Garden. It has become like a story, but the story of the flower art 'Karaki Ryugin' progresses as follows: Hirosaki Castle Botanical Garden East Gate → Flower Arch → Flower Water → Ascending Dragon → Apple Wish Tree → Towards Otemon. Appreciating the story deepens the experience.

title: Unexpected Encounter～予期せぬ出会い～
description:
Title: "Unexpected Encounter～予期せぬ出会い～"

Director: Kousuke Miyata
Visual: Shuji Hanbo
Photography: Eito Mars

Filming Locations:
Udonos Beach, Terasaki Fishing Port, Hato Pond, Okkinuku Coast, Sugarcane Fields, Ajinichie Shrine, Ajisaki, Izakaya Yasu, etc.

Filming Anecdote:
A journey to meet people on the island.
The Miyata crew arrived on Yoron Island on the afternoon of the first day with a 3-night, 4-day schedule, using Guest House KAI as a base. The filming locations were planned to be explored while experiencing the warmth of the people. The project aimed to create a tourism video that mixes the words written by writer Miyata, who felt and expressed his experiences on Yoron, the beautiful scenery of Yoron Island captured by Eito Mars, and the footage taken from a different perspective by Shuji Hanbo. The crew traveled around the island by rental car, capturing moments such as meeting islanders cultivating Yoron Island's water lemons at Udonos Beach, discovering sunset spots unknown to tourists, experiencing a tent sauna run by Michiyo Hida, who also assisted in the filming of Director Kumeda, and encountering islanders welcoming tourists with sanshin and conch shells at Hato Pond during a sunrise shoot. The filming progressed as connections with the people of Yoron were made. Based on these experiences, the text woven by Director Miyata was used in the subtitles of the work, culminating in a video piece that showcases both still photographs and live-action footage of the imagined landscapes.

title: 【新島ミライプロジェクト】210402 CX Live News it!
description: In spring 2021, this project aims to exchange plastic clothespins from all households on Niijima Island, Tokyo, for aluminum clothespins shaped like kusaya, called 'HOSSY'. By replacing plastic clothespins that deteriorate and break easily due to UV rays with the island's symbol, the kusaya-shaped clothespin, we hope to make the important industry of kusaya more familiar and, most importantly, to change to clothespins that will not break and be thrown away, leading to a lifestyle that does not produce plastic waste. Since the island has developed by receiving blessings from the sea, we want to create opportunities for each islander to think about 'What can we do for the natural environment now?'. In the future, we hope to borrow the power of Tokyo's treasure islands and also the strength of companies. Of course, we also plan to conduct crowdfunding ourselves to get as many people as possible to commit. We aim to expand our efforts in Niijima to all 11 islands of the Tokyo Islands and then spread this action to the islands of Japan. There are two aims: 1) To enhance understanding of Japanese food culture through 'dried fish (kusaya)' and pride in our hometown, and 2) To connect the often complex 'environmental issues' to a chain of awareness through unique initiatives. This is because it is a 'new island connected by new things'. A town that lives with the sea. It is an environmental action towards the 'Eco-Island Concept' that directly addresses marine environmental issues.

description:
On September 10, 2023 (Sunday), the Ginan Chijibai Performance will be held at the Ginan Town Fushiya Shishimai Hall. Following last year, the 'Ginan Chijibai Performance' allows audiences to enjoy 'Fushiya's Shishibai' along with other Shishibai and local Kabuki performances from within the prefecture. This year, the Seki City Shishimai Preservation Society and the Mino Kabuki Preservation Society will perform.

Kabuki 'Sannin Kichisa'

[Summary] Famous for the lines 'The moon is hazy over the white fish...' and 'This is a good omen for the spring,' this is a work by the playwright Kawatake Mokuami. On the night of Setsubun, Ojo Kichisa steals 100 ryo from a woman of the night by the Sumida River, but Obo Kichisa notices it, and the two fight over the money. A passing monk Kichisa mediates the dispute, and the three men with the same name reveal their true identities and become sworn brothers. The monk offers the 100 ryo to his father, Denkichi, but the bad money is thrown away. The 100 ryo ends up in the hands of the Obo, and Denkichi is killed by the Obo. Ojo and Obo meet the monk again, where the Obo learns for the first time that he killed the monk's father, and Ojo discovers that the woman of the night is the monk's sister. The two regret their sins and contemplate death...

description:
On September 10, 2023 (Sunday), the Ginan Local Theater Performance will be held at the Ginan Town Fushiya Shishimai Hall.

As one of the pre-events for the 39th National Cultural Festival and the 24th National Arts and Culture Festival for Persons with Disabilities, which will be held in Gifu Prefecture in 2024, the 'Ginan Local Theater Performance' was held again this year. This performance allows audiences to see 'Fushiya's Lion Dance' along with other lion dances and local kabuki from within the prefecture. This year, the Ginan Town Fushiya Shishimai Preservation Society, the Seki City Shishimai Preservation Society, and the Mino Kabuki Preservation Society performed.

　　Road Journey
　　Offering
　　Demon Exorcism
　　Lion Dance 'Keisei Awa no Naruto - Pilgrimage Song Segment'
　　
[Summary]
To search for the family treasure of the Tamaki family in Tokushima, the couple Jurobei and Oyu (the lion) leave their three-year-old daughter Otsuru at home and travel through various countries, but soon run out of money and become criminals. At the age of nine, Otsuru, longing to see her parents, sets out on a pilgrimage journey. One day, Oyu, who is hiding in Osaka, unexpectedly meets Otsuru, who is in pilgrimage attire. As Oyu listens to her story, she realizes that Otsuru is undoubtedly her daughter. Suppressing the urge to embrace her and introduce herself as her mother, Oyu advises Otsuru to return home, fearing that her daughter might be implicated in her crimes, but Otsuru, crying, pleads to stay with her, saying, 'I feel like I might be my mother.'

The “Poka Poka Nouen(Farm)” operated by Mr. Kushida, who has moved from Tokyo to Ayabe. "Poka Poka Nouen(farm)" is a renovation of an old folk house over 100 years old. Mr. Kushida grows rice and vegetables that are pesticide-free and fertilizer-free in the countryside where is full of nature. Also, from 2019, guests can enjoy the traditional "Goemon" style open-air bath which they can set the fire on their own. title: Fujimidaikogen, Nakatsugawa【中津川】
description: Fujimidaikogen is a beautiful mountain covered with bamboo grass at an elevation of 1,739m, located at the southern end of the Central Alps in the Ena mountain range. It is a popular hiking spot as you can drive up to the middle of the mountain, making it easily accessible. On clear days, you can enjoy the contrast between the green bamboo-covered slopes and the bright blue sky. At the summit, a magnificent 360-degree panorama awaits, overlooking Ena Mountain, the Northern Alps, the Southern Alps, and the Central Alps. In July, you can see the rare native plant Sasayuri, and from mid-October to early November, you can enjoy the fiery red mountain ranges. The climbing season is from late April to mid-November. Date of photography: July 18, 2021. For inquiries about tourism in Fujimidaikogen and Nakatsugawa, please contact the Nakatsugawa Tourism Association.

乗鞍岳を源とする多くの渓流と滝、池、湿原、さらに多種の獣、野鳥、昆虫などの野生生物が生息し、自然の多彩な表情が楽しめるスポットです。ひとたび足を踏み入れたら、偉大な自然のパワーを感じることができます。

title: ReVIEW! #Hida Takayama Ichinomiya Town
description: 飛騨一之宮観光協会会長　稲子盛雄さんが町の魅力をご紹介。一之宮町は、高山市の南部に位置する歴史と伝統が息づく地域。美しい自然に囲まれており、その環境を活かした農業体験や地元の人たちとのふれあい体験ができるグリーンツーリズムが盛んな地域です。なかでも、飛騨一宮水無神社は飛騨の国で最も格式高い神社とされ、地域に住む人たちの信仰を集め敬われています。他にも内閣府認定のどぶろく特区、樹齢1,100年の臥龍桜、分水嶺が見られる位山の散策やウィンタースポーツなど様々なジャンルを見て感じることができます。一之宮町に是非お越しください。（高山市街地から車で約２０分）

title: ReVIEW! #Hida Takayama Takane Town
description: 飛騨高根観光協会会長　小坂守さんが町の魅力をご紹介。高根町は高山市の南東に位置し、乗鞍岳と御嶽山を望み大自然に囲まれた高地にあります。長野県木曽地域に隣接しているため、歴史や文化、風俗に至るまで木曽の影響を色濃く受けており、飛騨の中でも異郷の地として知られています。高根町は木曽馬の産地だったことでも有名であり、馬の供養のために作られた石仏には、人と馬との物語が込められています。高根町では発酵食品に力を入れており、廃校を再利用したウイスキー蒸溜所は大きな話題を集めています。また、塩を一切使わず乳酸菌で漬けられた「すな」や、飛騨の郷土料理によく使われる田舎味噌なども盛んに作られています。この地域特有の涼しい夏と寒冷な冬の環境が、これらの発酵食品の育成に役立っています。その他には火畑そばやタカネコーン、野麦峠や御嶽山など様々な見どころがあるユニークな場所になっています。高根町に是非お越しください。（高山市街地から車で約５０分）

title: ReVIEW! #Hida Takayama Nyukawa Town
description: 千光寺住職　大下真海さんが町の魅力をご紹介。丹生川町は、高山市の北東部に位置する山岳地帯がある地域です。町を象徴するのが、日本百名山のひとつである乗鞍岳。標高3,000ｍ級の山にも関わらず、2,702mの畳平まで路線バスで行くことができるため、厳しいといわれる山岳の世界を子どもや女性でも気軽に体感することができます。７月から８月中旬にかけてバスターミナルのすぐ近くには天空のお花畑が広がり、希少な高山植物を観察できます。運が良ければ天然記念物のライチョウにも出会えるかもしれません。乗鞍岳の裾野に広がる五色ヶ原の森、観光鍾乳洞としては日本一標高が高い900ｍに位置する飛騨大鍾乳洞、飛騨の英雄・両面宿儺伝説、神社めぐり豊かな田園風景が残る里山など乗鞍岳に抱かれる町、丹生川町には多様な見どころがあります。荘川町に是非お越しください。（丹生川町は高山市街地から車で約15分／乗鞍岳山頂までは畳平から徒歩約90分）

title: The Town Where You Can Hear the Babbling Stream - Hida Kiyomi
description: 森に囲まれたおしゃれなカフェやレストランが点在する清見町は、洗練された雰囲気とのどかな自然が共存。町の中央を南北に縦断する全長64㎞の「飛騨美濃せせらぎ街道」は、格好のドライブルート。清流沿いで、初夏には新緑が輝きます。また、秋には紅葉の名所として知られ、標高差によって色づく場所が移り変わることで長期に渡り目を楽しませてくれます。

description: Utsue 48 Falls is a healing spot filled with negative ions, surrounded by countless waterfalls large and small. This natural park has been selected as one of Gifu Prefecture's top 50 famous waters. In the midst of rich nature, you can listen to the sound of water and take a leisurely stroll around 13 waterfalls. Among them, 'Otaki' is 18.8m high, and the white water falling down the rock face is very impressive! It takes about an hour from the starting point of the waterfall tour to the goal point, Shijuhachitaki Plateau. You can see the Northern Alps from the observation deck along the way. Please enjoy the beauty of nature that can only be enjoyed in Kokufu Town.

description: The 'Okura Falls Promenade' allows you to take a walk while admiring the large and small waterfalls known as 'Okura Hyakudaki.' This is a course that goes along the valley aiming for Okura Falls, which flows down with a drop of approximately 30 meters. Among the most recommended are the huge boulders that remain here and there. Kuguriiwa, which covers the promenade like a tunnel, is mysterious and impressive. Come and experience the magnificent power and beauty of nature. The best nature experience can be found in Kiyomi Town.

title: Cultural and Folklore Roots in Hida's Hometown #Gifu Prefecture #Hida Takayama "Kokufu Town"
description: 日本一面積が広い市である高山市は、町のすみずみまでたくさんの見どころに溢れています。飛騨高山を織りなすエリアにフォーカスしご紹介！知られざる逸話やその場所でしか味わえない体験など、飛騨高山ならではの多彩な魅力を掘り下げます。私たちの町、飛騨高山へようこそ。飛騨国府は、千数百年前、斐陀国(ひだのくに）の中心地「国府」として栄えました。風が香り、風が色づく、風の郷。土が香り、土が色づく、土の郷。季が香り、季が色づく、季の郷。飛騨路を北へたどると、なつかしい、ぬくもりに満ちた郷「飛騨国府」があります。初めて訪れた地なのに、なぜか不思議と懐かしさに包まれます。日本の原風景が色濃く残る歴史、民俗、自然をたずねて、この地になぜ「国府」が置かれたのかを実感できる旅となることでしょう。

title: 魅せる職人の技！春の #高山祭  #からくり人形　#飛騨高山
description: At the tip of a bridge over 8 shaku, a dragon god with a red face suddenly appears from a jar carried by a child, scattering paper snow and performing an angry dance. Skilled string manipulators operate the puppet with multiple strings, captivating the audience with the delicate yet bold performance of the puppet that seems almost alive.

Takayama City, the largest city in Japan, is an area rich in nature with a forest coverage rate exceeding 90%. description: Tsugaru nuri, the traditional crafts of Hirosaki city, Aomori prefecture, Japan. Tsugaru nuri, from over 300 years ago, have been handed down to the present by its long history up to today to the craftsmen’s patience, hard works and to their aesthetic eyes for beauty. From painting the surface of Cypress tree, and repetition of sharpening and polishing, the solid and elegant lacquer ware is after completing a long process of over forty steps for more than two months. It is also called “Baka nuri” meaning Foolish painting, because of the long careful process. This movie shows hand works of craftsmen, and four types of techniques 'Kara-nuri', 'Nanako-nuri', 'Monsha-nuri', and 'Nishiki-nuri' with the beauty of Tsugaru district.

Throughout the year, if the weather conditions are good, they kayak out into the sea of Kumano and serve fish they have caught themselves, maintaining a unique style of restaurant that is unimaginable in the city.

title: 青ノ詩を詠う - Pass the Baton -「市木木綿」唯一の職人の挑戦
description: The only craftsman of the traditional craft 'Ichiki Cotton' in Mihama Town, Mie Prefecture, Hirotaka Mukai, continues to weave 'Ichiki Cotton', designated as a traditional craft of Mie Prefecture, using a loom over 100 years old in the Ichiki district of Mihama Town once a week while running a family bedding store. The cotton weaving industry in the Ichiki district, which has continued since the Edo period, was branded as 'Ichiki Cotton' during the Meiji period, and at its peak, there were more than 40 factories. However, now only Mukai remains. At that time, he was forced to relocate from the factory he was renting, putting 'Ichiki Cotton' at risk of extinction. However, he turned this crisis into an opportunity by establishing the 'Ichiki Cotton Future Weaving Association' and decided to acquire his own factory to make it easier for future generations to take over the baton of 'Ichiki Cotton', pledging to give the new factory to an unseen successor for free. He decided to raise funds for the relocation, purchase, and renovation costs through crowdfunding. As a highlight of the crowdfunding rewards, he will create a new stripe called 'Mihama Blue', named after the town and reminiscent of the color of the town's sea. Thanks to the support of many people across the country who learned about the creation of the new stripe 'Mihama Blue', the situation of 'Ichiki Cotton', and Mukai's dedicated activities, the crowdfunding was a great success. After completing the relocation and renovation, Mukai began hosting 'traditional craft x tourism' tours to share the charm of 'Ichiki Cotton' with more people and to create a sustainable form of traditional craft, exploring the history and stories related to 'Ichiki Cotton' scattered around the new factory. His new challenge to weave 'Ichiki Cotton' into the future begins here.

title: Searching for Japan Blue - 青ノ詩を詠う
description: There exists a unique aesthetic sense among Japanese people regarding 'lush green.' 'Japan's blue' is made up of the 'blue' called blue and the 'green' called blue. The town where the 'blue' of the Pacific Ocean meets the 'blue' of the Kii Mountains is Kumano, a sacred place of syncretism of Shinto and Buddhism, located in Mihama Town, Mie Prefecture. In this town, we travel through 'Japan's blue.' The poet Haruo Sato reflected on the landscapes of his hometown Kumano and composed 'Bokyo Gogatsu Uta.' His poem, which captures the early summer scenery of his hometown with 'the sky is blue, the mountains are blue, the sea is blue,' skillfully encapsulated Kumano's 'blue.' The blue sea and sky of the Pacific Ocean, the blue mountains of the Kii Mountains, all color Kumano with 'blue.' 'The sea is blue, the wind is blue, and even the oranges are blue.' If Sato were alive, he might have composed a poem reflecting the scenery of Mihama Town in this way. In the mountains of the satoyama, there is a path of wind, the Kumano Kodo Fuden Pass. The morning mist, known as 'Fuden Oroshi,' rides the wind, and its mysterious appearance as it passes through the path reflects the 'blue' of Kumano's lush green mountains, dyeing the wind blue. Thus, the wind descends the satoyama, rushing through the gaps of the lush rice ears and the local specialty of Mihama Town, the blue oranges 'Gokuwase Unshu Mikan,' further dyeing itself blue. Eventually, the 'blue' of the mountains reaches the sea, merging with the 'blue' of the sea. Mihama is blue; the sea is blue; the mountains are blue; the sky is blue; the wind is blue; even the oranges are blue. Unravel and savor this town, woven together with 'Japan's blue,' and reweave it with your own sensibility. Then, try to compose your own poem of Mihama's 'blue.' description: Oroshi, located in Mihama Town, Mie Prefecture, is an area with many immigrants. Thanks to the beautiful satoyama scenery and the warm welcome from the local people, many people have been moving from the city in recent years. One day, when I visited Oroshi, I encountered a scene that looked so happy. Children run around the satoyama and play with nature. Adults are also enjoying their lives every day, realizing things they couldn't do in the city one by one. The people of Oroshi look enviable even to us immigrants. Mihama Town in Mie Prefecture is a town where mandarins can be harvested year-round, located along the Pacific Ocean at the southernmost tip of Honshu on the Kii Peninsula. Along the Pacific coast stretches the Nanri Ohama, about 22 km long. It is a prayer road loved by the common people since ancient times, and a World Heritage Site, the Kumano Kodo Ise Road. Thanks to the Kuroshio Current and the warm climate, various mandarins can be harvested throughout the year. The town has the mystical Kii Mountains and the magnificent Pacific Ocean, where the blue mountains meet the blue sea. Kumano has been called the 'land of resurrection.' In ancient Japan, it was believed that mountains were sacred places where gods and ancestors' spirits resided. Among them, Kumano is a sacred place where gods dwell, and those who visit will have their spirits revived and feel renewed. However, after that, we couldn't visit any other places, and due to this, we decided to move to Mihama Town, which felt like a fateful encounter. It took us about six months to make this decision. description: 御浜町に移住するまでは、こんな青いみかんがあることすら知らなかった。9月上旬から収穫される、御浜町の強い夏の日差しの下で育った、超極早生温州みかん。その日差しがみかんの糖度を高くするそうです。甘みと酸味の絶妙なバランスのみかんは非常に美味しかったです。今年は天気が良く、みかんの日焼けが心配だったそうですが、無事に出荷が始まりました。※みかんの表面の白い斑点はホワイトコートというカルシウム由来の日焼け防止剤です。超極早生温州みかんを皮切りに、御浜町では様々な種類のみかんが順次出荷されます。まさに、年中みかんのとれる町。そのみかんの収穫の様子を、御浜町のちせ農園を通してお伝えできればと思います。ちせ農園は現在、92歳になるちせさんからお孫さんに3年前に引き継がれたみかん農園になります。おばあちゃんに敬意を込めて名前はそのままにしたそうです。みかんを収穫する際のハサミの音色は心地よく、御浜町の秋の音だなと感じました。また、家族総出でみかんを収穫する様子はまさにこの町の家族の肖像のように思えました。三重県御浜町について、詳しくは下記Webサイトをご覧下さい↓ https://mihama-mie-townpromotion.jp/

title: 【移住のキッカケ】移住するキッカケになったお米を作る農家に会いにいく｜田舎暮らし｜熊野｜地方移住｜サステナブル
description: Something I always wanted to try. Cooking rice from the land with the water from the land where the rice was grown. I have tried various methods, but I have a feeling that this method will be the most delicious. Before moving, I visited Mihama Town in March this year and met a farmer by chance. He gave me rice because I came from Tokyo. When I returned to Tokyo and ate that rice, it was unbelievably delicious, and I was truly moved. However, a simple question arose. Wouldn't it be even more delicious if I cooked that rice with the water from the land where it was grown? After moving, I found out that the farmer was actually the father-in-law of one of my few acquaintances here, and I was able to observe the rice harvesting of that delicious rice this time. I only had an image of rice harvesting in autumn, but it was surprisingly before the Obon festival. And I also achieved my initial goal of cooking the rice from the land with the water from the land, making it a memorable day.

title: Matsunoyama Sustainable Dining in 美人林 2023
description:
Sustainability. An example of this remains in Japan's satoyama. The activities of the satoyama have been repeatedly disrupted and threatened by relentless heavy snowfall, yet they have risen again, inheriting the tradition while coexisting with nature. Matsunoyama Dining reconstructs this grand satoyama story through cuisine by the world-renowned 'TAKAZAWA'. This summer marks the fifth time that the satoyama story is told by 'TAKAZAWA', with special sponsorship from 'TELMONT', a French Champagne that supports the sustainable environment of the snow country.

Niseko 'TAKAZAWA' Chef Yoshitaka Takazawa / Nishiazabu 'Ma Cuisine' / Chef Ayasuke Ikejiri / Setagaya 'Signifiant Signifie' Chef Katsuaki Shiga / Shintomi Town 'Coulis' Chef Ryoma Orikasa / Sake Inn Tamakiya Chef Akira Kuriyama / Hinano Yado Chitose Chef Masamichi Yanagi

Special thanks: Hinano Yado Chitose / TAKAZAWA / Ma Cuisine / Signifiant Signifié / Coulis / Sake Inn Tamakiya / TELMONT / Snow Country Tourism Area / Matsunoyama Onsen LLC Manma / Tokamachi City Tourism Association

title: 【速報】#かざはやの里 の藤が見頃です！
description:
The wisteria at Kazahayano-sato in Tsu City, Mie Prefecture, is one of the representative wisteria spots in Mie Prefecture.

1800 wisteria plants of 10 varieties, including 'Shirokouhidanfuji', 'Murasakikouhidanfuji', 'Beni-fuji', 'Kuchibeni-fuji', 'Rokushaku-fuji', 'Kyushaku-fuji', 'Nagasaki-issai-fuji', 'Yaekokuryu-fuji', 'Kokuryu-fuji', and 'Shiranodafuji', bloom in 10,000㎡ of 10 types of wisteria trellises and 58,000㎡ of standing trees in the garden from late April to early May💜

Depending on the type of wisteria, some early bloomers have started to drop flowers, and there are many buds that will bloom soon☺

The seasonal flowers floating in the flower water are sure to be a great photo opportunity!

📅 April 13, 2024 (Sat) - May 6, 2024 (Mon) *Open every day
📍4096 Toki-cho, Tsu City, inside Ise Onsen Golf Club
⌚ 8:00 AM - 6:00 PM
🎫 Subject to change depending on blooming conditions
🚃 Shuttle buses operate from the east exit of Kintetsu 'Hisai Station' on weekends during the GW period
🚙 5 minutes by car from Ise Expressway 'Hisai IC', turn right at the Cosmos Shopping Center towards Kazahayai Pond, and turn left at the sign for the Social Welfare Corporation Seijukai 'Kazahaya'.

description: A god who guides good luck dwells! Power spot. Japan's oldest shrine rising in the forest. Tsubaki Shrine has been affectionately known as 'Tsubaki-san' since ancient times. It enshrines Sarutahiko Okami, known as the god of good luck. Many people pray for traffic safety, good health, and good business. The approach is lined with trees and a sacred atmosphere flows through it. In winter, camellia flowers bloom all over the temple grounds. The natural beauty that can be seen throughout the seasons is also one of the major attractions. There is also a matchmaking shrine and a power spot for fulfillment in love within the precincts! I would like to visit the shrine at the beginning of a new year.

title: 楽しもう！三重国立公園～
description:
Mie Prefecture has two national parks and two quasi-national parks.

The 'Ise-Shima National Park' features the Ise Grand Shrine and a ria coastline.
The 'Yoshino-Kumano National Park' is characterized by deep nature and history.
The 'Suzuka Quasi-National Park' boasts good transportation and the Suzuka Mountains and Yunoyama Onsen.
The 'Muro-Akame-Aoyama Quasi-National Park' allows you to enjoy the grandeur of mountains connected by valleys.

Each park has its own unique charm.
Why not enjoy the nature that can only be found in Mie's national and quasi-national parks?

description: The Ominokai Center, located at the gateway to the World Heritage town of Kumano, Mie, is right next to the Kumano Owasu Expressway and the Kumano Oodai Interchange. It is a facility where you can experience all of Kumano, offering seasonal meals and local specialties. It is adjacent to the 'Oni no K城', which is part of a World Heritage site and a national natural monument and scenic spot, and is also close to the Kumano Ancient Road 'Matsumoto Pass', making it easy to enjoy a walk on the Kumano Ancient Road!

title: 2019年4月5日オープン！「豪商のまち松阪　観光交流センター」を紹介します(松阪市)｜観光三重｜三重県の観光・旅行情報
description:
A tourist exchange center that comprehensively showcases various attractions of Matsusaka, including history, culture, and food, opened on April 5, 2019!

At the facility, you can learn about the history and cultural attractions of Matsusaka through exhibitions and video displays that incorporate the vibrancy of the Sangu Kaido, notable figures from Matsusaka, and Matsusaka merchants. You can also find information about tourist spots, local products, and restaurants in the city. By using the walking arrangement service (information terminal), you can create your own original sightseeing course.

As a guide for walking around the city, you can use the tourist exchange center to learn about history and culture, create your own route map, and then just enjoy yourself to the fullest! You can also buy souvenirs at the center, so please stop by again at the end!

title: I visited the national scenic spot and natural monument 'Oni no K城' (Kumano City) | Tourism Mie | Mie Prefecture's tourism and travel information
description: Oni no K城, a natural art formed by uplift, weathering, and wave erosion, stretches for 1 km facing Kumano Bay and is designated as a national scenic spot and natural monument. At the summit, there are ruins of a castle from the Sengoku period, and a hiking course is established that connects to the Kumano Kodo and Matsumoto Pass. From the observation deck known as the 'Oni's Viewing Platform,' you can see the entire Kumano Bay.

title: FARM STAY in JAPAN! - Traditional Japanese travel experience in Akita
description:
What better way is there to experience Japanese culture than being invited into a local farmers home to hang out and stay the night? On our recent trip to Akita (秋田県), we did a farm homestay in the humble town of Odate (大館市). We stayed with Yamauchi-san and his wife and together we cooked the local cuisine - Kiritanpo (切りたんぽ).

Kiritanpo is essentially mashed rice, cooked on a stick over an open fire, and then either eaten with a delicious miso glaze, or put in another meal, such as a hotpot - perfect for a chilly winter night! We had a quick trip to an onsen, and afterwards we stayed up late into the night having drinks, laughing and enjoying each others company.

The next day Yamauchi gave us a personal tour of his town, giving us all the insider knowledge that you couldn't discover by yourself as a tourist. We even got to see and pet the famous Akita Inu's (秋田犬)! Even with our limited Japanese speaking ability, Yamauchi-san and his wife were incredibly accommodating and we can't thank them enough for such a fun experience.

If you are ever visiting Japan in winter we would highly recommend this experience! We stayed in Ganiba Onsen in Akita and during our time at the ryokan we also got to experience a traditional multi-course Japanese dinner and breakfast.

High quality lumber processing technique of shipwrights used to serve the powerful navy of Awa-Han (feudal domain/a part of present Tokushima) greatly in the Edo Period (1603–1868), and the technique has been passed down through the generations. A carpentry skill called Mokuhari (thin wood sheet craft) is utilized and beautiful paintwork is applied to Yusanbako. description:
【🍁日本遺産・水遺産「永源寺」⛩】
滋賀県東近江市に佇む「永源寺（えいげんじ）」は、650年以上の歴史を誇る臨済宗永源寺派の大本山です。

境内には、国内屈指の大きさを誇るヨシ葦屋根の方丈（本堂）や県指定有形文化財があります。

深い自然に抱かれた幽境に栄える伽藍は四季折々の姿を楽しむことができ、秋に見られる境内を埋め尽くすほどの真っ赤な紅葉🍁は関西有数の紅葉の名所として全国から多くの参拝者が訪れます。

普段は一般の方の立ち入りを禁止している場所もボランティアガイドと一緒なら特別に見学することができます。紅葉が古刹に映える永源寺の魅力を、ぜひ映像でお楽しみください。

https://ja.biwako-visitors.jp/spot/detail/2532

description: 【The Town of Railways - Yokokawa】 The line between Takasaki and Yokokawa opened in 1885, and the line between Naoetsu (Niigata Prefecture) and Karuizawa opened in 1888. The 11.2 km section between Yokokawa (Gunma Prefecture) and Karuizawa (Nagano Prefecture) opened in just a year and a half in 1893. The town of Yokokawa became the gateway for travelers crossing the pass. 'Toge no Kamameshi' was first sold at Yokokawa Station on the Shin'etsu Line on February 1, 1958, and has sold approximately 170 million units, making it a representative product of station bento. The ceramic container that inspired the birth of Toge no Kamameshi was adopted in response to customers' requests for 'warm bento' during long train journeys. The warm rice is served in a Mashiko-yaki earthenware pot, accompanied by nine ingredients such as chicken, bamboo shoots, shiitake mushrooms, burdock, chestnuts, and apricots. The contents and wrapping change with the seasons and events, delighting both tourists and locals. The 'station soba and udon' at Yokokawa Station and Karuizawa Station are also recommended.

description: Official website: https://bit.ly/3koX8Qf Official Instagram: https://bit.ly/3XgZuzh Kikai Island, made of coral, boasts a beautiful natural environment. It is a nature-rich island where the blue of the beautiful sea and the green of the land overlap. The island's culture, relaxed island time, and encounters with kind islanders create a wonderful journey filled with joy. ■ What is Kikai Island Kikai Island is located about 380 km south of Kagoshima and 25 km east of Amami Oshima. It is an uplifted coral reef island floating on the ocean where the Pacific Ocean and the East China Sea meet. Most of the island is uplifted coral reef, and it is a scientifically valuable island that continues to rise at an average of 2 mm per year. The island is covered with sugarcane fields, and the brown sugar and brown sugar shochu made from sugarcane are local specialties. It is also known as the largest producer of white sesame in Japan. Within Kikai Island, there are many famous spots, including Hyakunodai Park, one of the ten scenic spots of Amami, beautiful Sugirabeach, Hawaii Beach, and ancient coral stone walls. In recent years, it has also attracted attention as a diving spot.

title: 摩周湖早朝雲海 / Sea of Clouds Over Lake Mashu in the Early Morning
description:
Website: http://untouchedhokkaido.jp/ FACEBOOK: https://www.facebook.com/untouchedhokkaido/ Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/untouched_hokkaido/?hl=en

Around 20 minutes by car from Kawayu Hot Springs is Lake Mashu Viewpoint No. 3. Arrive here between sunrise and around 8:00 AM and you might see an incredible sea of clouds. The clouds covering the sky change from one movement to the next - you won't be able to tear your eyes away! The scene is completed by waves of clouds that flow over Lake Mashu from the surrounding mountains. June to September is the best time to see the sea of clouds in Teshikaga Town. Lake Mashu Viewpoint No. 3 is the best vantage point, at over 100m higher than Viewpoint No. 1. If you're lucky, you'll see a "double sea of clouds" around you, with clouds covering both Lake Mashu and Lake Kussharo! Make sure you check the best time of morning and viewing conditions in advance, as it changes depending on the season and the weather.

title: 釧路川源流クルーズ・鏡の間
description: The Kushiro River is the only river that flows out of Lake Kussharo. It runs through Kushiro Shitsugen Wetland and out to sea. A short distance to the side of the Kushiro River is a magical spot called Kagami no Ma. Kagami no Ma is Japanese for 'mirror room' and you'll see why as soon as you see how clear this spring is. The water remains below 10°C all year round, and the area offers a vastly different scene from the Kushiro River nearby. With its cool air, crystal-clear water and lush greenery, Kagami no Ma will captivate you.

title: 和琴半島一周カヌークルーズ
description: Wakoto Peninsula is a peninsula that is about 3km around, jutting into a lake with a circumference of 57km. Its name comes from the Ainu phrase 'wakkochi', which means 'the narrow part of a fish's tail'. The peninsula is a fascinating volcanic area, with hot springs everywhere and an area called Oyakotsu Jigoku (Oyakotsu Hell) at the tip of the peninsula, where plumes of smoke rise from the ground. Covered with deep forest, Wakoto Peninsula offers new natural splendor with each season: North Japanese hill cherry blossoms in spring, new greenery in early summer, colorful foliage in autumn. On a sunny day, Lake Kussharo is at its clearest, offering a view that will take your breath away. After you paddle around the peninsula, Mrs. Hiratsuka will serve you a hearty homemade lunch near the stunning Oyakotsu Jigoku. Made with local ingredients from Teshikaga and the surrounding area, every option will have you smacking your lips in satisfaction. The heartfelt hospitality you'll receive will make this the best canoe cruise you've ever been on.

title: 阿寒湖・阿寒川フィッシング
description: Lake Akan is famous for its marimo moss balls and is surrounded by untouched nature. It's also home to an abundance of native trout species, making it a beloved spot for fly fishing and lure fishing enthusiasts. Fishing is banned until April 30 each year to protect the fish population, but the period from May 1 until autumn is an angler's paradise! Even beginners will find it easy to catch rainbow trout, Japanese char, and kokanee in Lake Akan. Be aware that the area from the mouth of the Akan River at Lake Akan to the Yukan Bridge is a catch-and-release area - the first in Hokkaido (designated in 2003). A recreational fishing charge of JPY1,500 per day applies (to be paid in advance).

title: Chikurouen Flagship Store / 竹老園東家総本店
description: Chikurouen's flagship store is one of the oldest soba noodle restaurants in Hokkaido. With a history of over 140 years, this specialist restaurant has honed its skills and is still striving to improve on its authentic local noodles. Kushiro soba noodles stand out from the rest - they're green! That's because they're made from new buckwheat. The founder of Chikurouen is said to have wanted every customer to enjoy soba noodles made from new buckwheat, and that tradition is still alive today.

title: Untouched Hokkaido ダイジェスト(Summer)
description:
Website: http://untouchedhokkaido.jp/ FACEBOOK: https://www.facebook.com/untouchedhokkaido/ Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/untouched_hokkaido/?hl=en

Historically and geographically, Eastern Hokkaido is a unique place that, while being part of Japan, is located on the North American Plate, resulting in a rich variety of rare plant species. It is here that one can encounter rare wildlife, and the national parks of Japan, where many creatures live, have been preserved by the local people who have coexisted with nature for a long time, creating a place where 'nature remains untouched (Untouched Hokkaido)'. Eastern Hokkaido is connected by rich clear streams and is home to the elegant and beautiful Tancho, a special natural monument of Japan. In the language of the indigenous Ainu people of Hokkaido, the Tancho is called Sarorunkamuy (the god that lives in the marsh). Water nurtures life and transforms into various forms as if enchanted.

title: Mt. Io:Untouched Hokkaido/硫黄山
description:
Teshikaga Town: Mt. Io

Stand inches away from the pulse of the earth. With the distinctive smell of sulfur and alpine plants at much lower altitudes than they usually grow, Mt. Io is like a scene from another planet. Mt. Io is located around 3km from Kawayu Hot Springs, and is called Atosa-nupuri (bare mountain) in Ainu. To this day, sulfur plumes rise from various areas of the mountain, with an incredible rumbling sound. Large-scale sulfur mining once took place here, which played a significant role in Teshikaga Town's development. Parking is free during the winter (late November to early April). The Kushiro area is home to the natural habitat of the red-crowned crane, a designated special natural monument that was once called “sarorun kamuy”, which means “spirits that live in the marshlands”, by the native Ainu people.

Untouched Hokkaido
Eastern Hokkaido has a history and geography all of its own. Despite its location in Japan, it is actually on the North American tectonic plate, and as a result it is full of extremely rare plant life. Eastern Hokkaido locals have coexisted for generations with the area's rare wildlife and the nature in the national parks that those animals call home, and as a result there are many natural areas that are untouched by human hands.

The mother of the gods, Izanami Nomikoto When Izanagi Nomikoto visited her, Mt. Tateeboshi, It's night, so she lit her comb and used it as a light. title: Sanin海岸 - 山陰海岸
description: In the Chugoku region of Japan, the north of the Chugoku Mountains has been called Sanin(mountain’s yin) and the south has been called Sanyo(mountain’s yang) for a long time. When naming a place, it is based on the idea of ancient China that the north and south of the mountain are represented by yin and yang, and the north and south of the river are represented by yang and yin. This is because in the northern hemisphere, where the sun rises in the southern sky, the north of the mountain is in the shadow and the south is in the sun. In the case of rivers, there are lands in China that are described as Yinyang in the north and south of the river, such as Rakuyo (the area north of the river called Luoyang) and Huaiyin (south of the river called Huai’an). In the case of rivers, the light from the south bounces off the surface of the river, illuminating the north of the river, and objects in the south cast shadows on the surface of the river. The coast of the San'in(mountain’s yin) region on the north side of the Chugoku Mountains faces the Sea of Japan. Enjoy the scenic landscape of the San'in coast formed by the rough waves of the Sea of Japan generated by the wind blowing from the continent.

description: 御祭神は古代豪族 物部氏 初代宇摩志麻遅命(うましまじのみこと)。宇摩志麻遅命は邇芸速日命(にぎはやひのみこと)の子にあたられ、神武天皇の東征の際、長髄彦(ながすねひこ)を討ち、後に物部氏を率いて皇城守護の任に就いたとされています。創建から数えて1500年以上の歴史があり、ご本殿は出雲大社に次ぐ二番目の大きさで、春日造りの巨大神殿となっています。御神紋『ひおい鶴』は宇摩志麻遅命が鶴に乗って降臨されたという故事に基づいた御神紋で、日本唯一の御神紋と言われています。

title: Tokyo Akasaka Hikawa Shrine - 東京 赤坂 氷川神社
description: Akasaka Hikawa Shrine, which counts a thousand years since its enshrined. Deity: Susano-no-mikoto, Kushinadahime-no-mikoto, Okuninushi-no-mikoto. In the past, Kushinadahime-no-mikoto was rescued by Susano-no-mikoto from the sacrifice of Yamata-no-Orochi, and later became the wife of Susano-no-mikoto. Okuninushi is the descendant of couple, and is also the main deity of Izumo Taisha as a national creation god. It is said to have originated from Hikawa in Izumo Province, which was the stage for exterminating Yamata-no-Orochi. It begins when a monk who was traveling to Togoku in 951, in his dream, responded to the announcement from the deity when he spent the night at the present Akasaka 4th street and worshiped here. description:
○Best time to visit: Late April to early May

○Shooting location: Inami Betsuin Zuisen-ji
○Address: 3050 Inami, Nanto City, Toyama Prefecture, 932-0211, Japan
○Phone number: 0763-82-0004
○URL: https://inamibetuin-zuisen-ji.amebaownd.com/

○Overview
Zuisen-ji has suffered three major fires in the years Tensho 9, Hōreki 12, and Meiji 12, resulting in the loss of its buildings (garan). However, it has been rebuilt each time with the support and wishes of the local community. During these reconstructions, skilled carpenters from the main temple in Kyoto were dispatched to directly oversee and guide the rebuilding, passing on their exceptional techniques to the carpenters of Inami. The traditional craft of Inami carving, which has continued to this day, is believed to have been created through the harmony and fusion of techniques learned from Kyoto's excellent traditional temple architecture and sculpture, and the skills cultivated by Inami carpenters during the reconstruction of Zuisen-ji. For this reason, Inami Betsuin Zuisen-ji is said to be the birthplace of Inami carving.

*Source: Inami Betsuin Zuisen-ji website

title: Trip to Nanto City, Toyama Prefecture - 福野夜高祭り　～引き合い（通称：ケンカ）～
description: The Fukuno Yotaka Festival (福野夜高祭り) is a spring festival at Fukuno Shinmeisha Shrine, with the Yotaka Festival on the nights of May 1st and 2nd serving as the welcoming ceremony for the gods, and the main festival on the 3rd featuring the procession of portable shrines and floats. It was once believed that the gods did not always reside at the shrine but only came during the festival, which is why the welcoming ceremony is held. During the evening festival, the Yotaka lanterns are paraded, and the sounds of the Yotaka drums and the spirited shouts of the young men resonate in the spring night sky. On the 2nd, the highlight event known as 'Hiki-ai' (commonly referred to as 'Kenka') takes place. The deity of the Shinmeisha Shrine is said to be a goddess who loves fights, and it is believed that the more intense the Hiki-ai, the more pleased she becomes. This event begins when the ascending and descending lanterns pass each other on Kamimachi Street. In the past, when candles were used, there were instances of flames catching. Once all the neighborhoods have completed their parades, a concluding ceremony called 'Shanshan' is held. Each neighborhood gathers at the bank intersection to report the safe completion of the festival and perform a hand-clapping ritual. The main festival on May 3rd features the floats from four neighborhoods (Kamimachi, Shinmachi, Uramachi, Yokomachi) leading to the Shinmeisha Shrine, accompanied by the portable shrine parading through the town, where the parishioners scatter purifying salt to welcome the procession.

title: Trip to Nanto City, Toyama Prefecture
description: The Fukuno Yotaka Festival (福野夜高祭り) is held on April 30th every year at the JR Fukuno Station square (rotary). The highlight is the Bunkyu giant lantern, which is about 15 meters tall and more than twice the size of the giant lanterns still passed down in the Fukuno area of Nanto City. It recreates the scale of those made in an era without utility poles. The evening festival, starting on May 1st, features the procession of the Yotaka lanterns, with the sounds of Yotaka drums and the spirited shouts of the young men echoing. The biggest attraction is the 'hiki-ai' (fight) that begins around 11 PM on the 2nd, where the young men break each other's lanterns with lively clappers. The intense competition captivates the audience. During the main festival, four town floats visit the Shinmei Shrine, and the portable shrine parades through the town.

Passed down through generations in the Gokayama region, Kokiriko is a simple folk song and dance with roots in a performing art called Dengaku, which originated around 1,400 years ago during the Taika Reforms. Believed to be the oldest folk song in Japan, its name appears in many ancient documents.

title: プライベートビーチでの海女バトラーとのプレミアムディナー
description:
■Activity details■
Ama are female freedivers who catch seafood such as abalone and sea urchin. Ama fishing, which has been a tradition in Shima, Mie for over 2,000 years, is designated as an important intangible folk cultural property. With over 200 active ama, it is one of the few places in the country where this type of fishing is still practiced. The average ama age is 65!

This program offers participants the chance to get their fill of Shima accompanied by energetic ama. First, participants will head out on a boat with the ama to experience their traditional basket fishing technique used to collect a variety of fresh seafood. Next they'll enjoy a special dinner made with the freshly caught seafood on a private beach. The ama serve as their own private butlers for an unforgettable experience.

title: 長谷園、200年の日本の食文化の歴史を持つ伊賀焼の窯
description: ■Activity details■Located in northern Mie prefecture in a quiet area where you can see chimneys poking up around town is Marubashira, the Iga ware village. The pottery crafted here is highly flame resistant, and since long ago, clay pots used for cooking on open flames and teapots have been made in this village. Nagatanien, one of the potteries of Iga ware, has continued to carry on the techniques of this craft since the workshop's founding in 1832, making pieces that are highly valued both in Japan and abroad. This program offers participants the chance to go on a special tour of the climbing kilns with the eighth generation head of Nagatanien while listening to secret stories about Iga ware, and to try cooking in a famous Nagatanien clay pot. Don't miss the chance to try some delicious rice prepared in this unique piece of pottery!

title: 熊野古道の馬越峠を歩く、ユネスコ世界遺産
description:
■Activity details■
Long ago, it was popular for people from all across Japan to walk hundreds of kilometers to tour sacred sites such as Ise Grand Shrine and Kumano Sanzan (the Three Grand Shrines of Kumano). Many travelers walked the perilous Magose Pass, which is part of the Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range that leads to Kumano Sanzan. The beautiful stone paved path leading deep into the forest has been lovingly maintained by locals for centuries, and still looks as it did long ago. This program offers participants the chance to dress in travel garb recreated from ukiyo-e prints and historic documents and walk the Magose Pass just as ancient travelers did. Partial proceeds from the program are used to preserve the stone paving and keep the scenery in pristine condition for future generations.

title: 志摩市でのユニークな真珠ジュエリー体験
description: ■Activity details■ Shima, Mie is the birthplace of pearl cultivation. Thanks to abundant ocean resources and time-honored techniques, Shima pearls are known as being some of the highest quality around the world. This program offers participants the chance to visit a pearl farm to learn about the cultivation techniques in person while talking with artisans. They'll also have the chance to collect pearls from oysters and the very rare chance to seed oysters, learning just how difficult the process of pearl cultivation truly is. Finally, participants will use the pearls they collect to make a one-of-a-kind piece of jewelry.

title: 山城の地での本格的な忍者体験
description:
■Activity details■
Long ago, many mountain castles were built in Iga, where the ninja were valued for their ability to move swiftly when fighting in mountainous terrain. This program offers participants an authentic ninja experience to learn ninjutsu at the site of a mountain castle, just like the ninja of old. The introductory course teaches breathing techniques, mystic hand signs, and fundamental walking techniques based on Iga ninjutsu at an indoor dojo. After lunch, participants will try swinging a sword in the forest, using a grappling hook, concealment techniques, and more while walking through the site of a mountain castle which records say was used for actual ninja training. This program is designed by the Japan Ninja Council, and is part of a rare domestic workshop that offers continuous advancement based on a systematic curriculum.

Step away from the noise and find your own silence. Timeless beauty in every moment of life.

title: KYOTO SERENDIPITY - イザベラ・バード

As she noted in her book Unbeaten Tracks in Japan: "The Japanese are wonderfully gentle, courteous, and good-tempered." Discover the universal virtues she admired—a timeless beauty found in every moment of life.
