description:
The official website of Kanra Town Hall is here: https://www.town.kanra.lg.jp/

"Discover new charms by viewing the town from the sky!" With this concept, we will be shooting videos.
This time, we filmed the scenic spot "Rakuzan-en" located in Kanra Town!
We also filmed the light-up event "Kirameki" held at Rakuzan-en from April 20 to April 30, so please take a look at that as well.

Rakuzan-en is...
A garden created by the Oda clan in the early Edo period, it is a pond-style strolling garden with a borrowed scenery. Centered around a pond with placed scenic stones, it creates a varied terrain with "Nakajima" and "Tsukiyama". It features multiple tea houses, including "Ume no Chaya" and the nationally rare pentagonal-shaped "Koshikake Chaya", and the garden paths are also ingeniously designed.

Shooting equipment: 【DJI】Phantom 4 Pro V2.0
Editing: Adobe Premiere Pro 2019
Viewpoint: Rakuzan-en
648-2 Obata, Kanra Town, Kanra District, Gunma Prefecture

The hiking trails to Tsukuba Mountain allow visitors to enjoy historical towns that retain the atmosphere of the Edo period, with signposts and traditional storehouses. The mountain offers year-round opportunities for hiking and enjoying nature. Additionally, with the use of cable cars and ropeways, anyone from children to the elderly can easily reach the summit and enjoy the beautiful views.

title: Enchanting Tokyo HACHIJOJIMA Island (Full ver.)／八丈島
description: Hachijojima Island, which is less than an hour’s flight from Tokyo, is an island where you can enjoy the great outdoors. With one of the highest precipitation rates in Japan, Hachijojima has its own unique environment including giant ferns and potholes carved into the rock by ever-flowing spring water. On the island, you can enjoy hiking as well as running and fishing. After enjoying physical activities, visitors can relax in a natural hot spring surrounded by rich nature, making it the perfect environment for a refreshing weekend getaway.

The video “Enchanting Tokyo AOGASHIMA Island” introduces the unique landscape of the island, including the world-famous double caldera and geothermic “hingya” steam eruptions. The video also explores the island’s way of life and beliefs that coexist in harmony with nature.

Centered on 'Japanese food,' now registered as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, enjoy dishes that have existed since the Edo period, including sushi, eel, soba and tempura. The theme of food continues with the tastes of the people, such as ramen noodles and local bars, and a selection of Japanese confections. With beautiful shots of delicious food, chefs showing off their talents and sweets that'll have you salivating at just a glance, you can enjoy everything aside from actually eating the food! In Chuo City, one of the greatest gourmet cities in the world, experience a rich variety of Japanese food.

title: Türkiye-Japonya zamanı aşan dostluk ～ Ertuğrul Fırkateyni ile başlayan dostluk bağı ～
description: 1890年（明治23年）9月16日に、オスマン帝国から日本へ初めて友好使節として「エルトゥールル艦」が送られました。任務を終えた艦は帰路の途中で和歌山県の大島地域（現在の串本）で岩に衝突し、沈没しました。この悲劇的な事故で587人の海軍士官が命を落としました。大島の人々の救助活動により69人が救出されました。この「エルトゥールル事故」は、その後、日本とトルコの友好関係の始まりとなりました。この事故から1年後、トルコの記念碑が建立され、その前で式典が行われました。それ以来、トルコ大使館と串本町の共催で5年ごとに大規模な式典が行われています。2015年6月6日には125周年の追悼式典が行われ、串本と和歌山はトルコとの関係をさらに深めました。

Nikko (日光, Nikkō) is a town at the entrance to Nikko National Park, most famous for Toshogu, Japan's most lavishly decorated shrine and the mausoleum of Tokugawa Ieyasu, the founder of the Tokugawa shogunate.

Nikko had been a center of Shinto and Buddhist mountain worship for many centuries before Toshogu was built in the 1600s, and Nikko National Park continues to offer scenic, mountainous landscapes, lakes, waterfalls, hot springs, wild monkeys and hiking trails.

title: Chair Lift Ride at Mount Takao (Ascend) | Japan's Steepest Slope | 高尾山　チェアリフト
description:
Mount Takao (高尾山, Takao-san) is a mountain in the city of Hachiōji, Tokyo, Japan. It is protected within Meiji no Mori Takao Quasi-National Park.

Standing 599 metres (1,965 ft) tall and located within an hour of downtown Tokyo, it is a popular hiking spot, with eight hiking courses and more than 2.5 million annual visitors. The Tama Forest Science Garden is also located at the mountain's base.

THE CHAIR LIFT RIDE

In addition to the cable car Mt. Takao also has a chair lift that you can ride to the midway point of the mountain! The ride time is about 12 minutes so why not enjoy an aerial trip through the mountains? The distance from “Sanroku Station” at the foot of the mountain to “Sanjo Station” in the middle is about 872m, which is shorter than the distance the cable car travels (The cable car travels a total of 1,020m).

title: Autumn at Shinobazu Pond | Boat Ride | Ueno Park | 不忍池　上野公園
description: Come and join us as we show you the relaxing view of autumn at Shinobazu Pond. Shinobazu no Ike which is found within the Ueno Park in Taito Ku Tokyo, is historically prominent and usually appears in Japanese history and works of art. If you wanna ride a boat on the boat pond, make sure to wear a mask, sanitize your hands and let the staff check your temperature. Ticket machine is available at the entrance. The price of boat ride varies with the type of boat you wanna ride on to. A Cycle boat costs 700 yen, maximum of 2 adults for 30 mins. Swan boat costs 800 yen maximum 3 adults for 30 mins. While a row boat costs 500 yen maximum of 3 adults for 30mins. Situated in the south of Ueno Park, the pond is divided in three sections. The Lotus Pond (蓮の池, Hasu no Ike), the Boat Pond (ボートの池, Bōto no Ike) and the third called Cormorant Pond (鵜の池, U no Ike). The pond has a circumference of about 2 km and a surface area of about 1,100,000 sq meters. It hosts several dozens of types of migratory and stationary birds, whose number at times is over ten thousand. Among them particularly numerous are tufted ducks, pochard, and northern pintails. The pond also contains numerous species of fish, and the lotuses of Lotus Pond, which are grown fully in summer, cover the entire surface of the water, hiding it almost completely.

title: Fujikawaguchiko Autumn Leaves Festival 2021 | 富士河口湖紅葉まつり 2021 | Mt Fuji Bound
description:
#fujikawaguchikoautumnleavesfestival2021 #fujikawaguchiko #autumnfestival #japan #富士河口湖紅葉まつり #mtfuji #mybestjapanmoments #visitjapanjp #falfoliage #autumninjapan #viaggiatotravelservices

Fuji Kawaguchiko Autumn Leaves Festival (富士河口湖紅葉まつり) is one of the most popular autumn events in Japan which is annually held at the northern shore of Lake Kawaguchi, one of the Fuji Five Lakes. This year’s festival is held from Oct.30 to Nov.23 2021.

The event features colourful autumn leaves which stretch around Lake Kawaguchi area, and during daytime, the beautiful scenery can be enjoyed with the amazing view of Mt Fuji on the background.

The festival is centered around the “Momiji Corridor” or Momiji Kairo and is held from 9:00 in the morning. While the light up starts from sunset to 10:00 at night.

The most popular autumn leaves spot is the Momiji Kairo (もみじ回廊) a.k.a. the Maple Corridor.

This is a walkway lined by over 60 maple trees with autumn colour leaves. The trees with red, yellow and orange leaves stretch for about 2km, displaying the stunning scenery.

During the festival, there will be food stalls selling seasonal foods and drinks, as well as small stores selling local products and souvenirs. oh and by the way, most of these souvenirs are hand painted and handmade.

The Tokyo Imperial Palace (皇居, Kōkyo, literally 'Imperial Residence') is the main residence of the Emperor of Japan. It is a large park-like area located in the Chiyoda district of the Chiyoda ward of Tokyo and contains several buildings including the main palace (宮殿, Kyūden), some residences of the Imperial Family, an archive, museums and administrative offices.

It is built on the site of the old Edo Castle. The total area including the gardens is 1.15 square kilometres (0.44 sq mi). During the height of the 1980s Japanese property bubble, the palace grounds were valued by some to be more than the value of all of the real estate in the state of California.

title: Yumenoshima Tropical Greenhouse Dome | Annual Halloween Pumpkin Month | 夢の島熱帯植物館| ハロウィーンのカボチャ
description:
Today we’re gonna explore the Yumenoshima Tropical Greenhouse Dome.

The Yumenoshima Tropical Greenhouse Dome was created to cover this broad theme of “the relationship between tropical plants and our lives.” Enjoy the exotic scenery created by the wide variety of tropical plants in the large greenhouse. Learn about the plants and the tropics in the Movie Theater, Information Gallery, and Exhibition Hall. Take a full tour of the museum and learn about the relationship between tropical plants and human life without even realizing it. Guided tours are offered on Saturdays, Sundays, national holidays, and during long vacations. Enjoy a fun tour while learning in detail about the plants in the greenhouse.

"The Yumenoshima Tropical Greenhouse Dome (夢の島熱帯植物館, Yumenoshima Nettai Shokubutsukan), also sometimes called the Yumenoshima Tropical Plant Dome, is a botanical garden located at 3-2, Yumenoshima, Kōtō, Tokyo, Japan. It is operated by the Tokyo Metropolitan Park Association and open daily except Mondays; an admission fee is charged.

The greenhouse was established in 1988 in Yumenoshima ("Dream Island") Park, a reclaimed landfill and dumping ground in Tokyo Bay. Its three domes currently contain about 1,000 species of tropical and semitropical plants. The A Dome features rain forest with ferns and waterfall, B Dome represents a tropical village, and C Dome contains vegetation of the Ogasawara Islands. There is also a small carnivorous plant room.

The domes' plant collections include palms, orchids, aquatic plants, Pandanus, Hevea brasiliensis, Samanea saman, Barringtonia racemosa, Satakentia liukiuensis, Cyathea lepifera, C. mertensiana, C. spinulosa, and Dicksonia antarctica." -Wikipedia

Yumenoshima Tropical Greenhouse Dome is celebrating their annual Halloween Pumpkin Month from end of September to First of November. You will see their Halloween theme all around the area, inside the museum and on their front lawn or garden are giant pumpkins where you and your kids can play around. Enjoy and shoot lovely Autumn and Halloween photos which will be a great memorabilia for you and your kids!

10 minute walk from Shin-Kiba Station, which is 10 minutes from Tokyo Station on the Keiyo Line. Also accessible on the Yurakucho Line.

Fees: Adults 250 yen, Ages 65 yrs old and older 120 yen, Ages 13–15 yrs old 100 yen. Under 12 yrs old are FREE!

title: Fuji Shibazakura Festival 2021 | Mt. Fuji Tour | 富士芝桜
description: Have you ever seen an enormous field carpeted with pink or white or purple flowers? If not, then we will show you this fantastic and mesmerizing Fuji Shibazakura Festival 2021 in Yamanashi, Japan, included in our Mt. Fuji Tour this Spring Season. Shibazakura 富士芝桜 is a Japanese term for Pink Phlox or Moss Phlox. The festival is open from 8 in the morning until 3 in the afternoon. Entrance fees range from 250yen per each child and 800 yen for adults. During these days, the pink moss and all the flowers in the festival were not yet in full bloom. So as you can see, the fields are not yet fully covered with pink moss flowers. but during the full bloom days, its really mesmerizing with mt fuji on the background. The festival is typically held from mid April through early June. The best time to see the flowers varies from year to year but usually falls into the first three weeks of May. Approximately 800,000 stalks of shibazakura of five varieties are on display, producing delightful fields of pink, white and purple colors in different hues. There are also food trucks which offer a wide variety of menus and food to go as you enjoy the beauty of the scenery around you stalls selling pots of pink moss, shibazakura-themed souvenirs, food and local produce complete the experience. title: Shiraito no Taki | Shiraito Falls | 白糸の滝 | Mt. Fuji Tour
description: Shiraito Falls (白糸の滝, Shiraito no taki) is a waterfall in Fujinomiya, Shizuoka Prefecture, near Mount Fuji, Japan. It is part of Fuji-Hakone-Izu National Park and has been protected since 1936 as a Japanese Natural Monument. The falls were regarded as sacred under the Fuji cult. Another waterfall, the Otodome Falls is approximately a five-minute walk away. The Shiraito Falls is listed as one of 'Japan’s Top 100 Waterfalls', in a listing published by the Japanese Ministry of the Environment in 1990. It was also selected by the Tokyo Nichi Nichi Shimbun and Osaka Mainichi Shimbun as one of the 100 Landscapes of Japan in 1927. In 2013 the waterfall was added to the World Heritage List as part of the Fujisan Cultural Site.

title: Narusawa Ice Cave | Mt. Fuji Tour | 鳴沢氷穴 | Narusawa Hyōketsu
description: The Narusawa 'Hyoketsu' Ice Cave is located at the east entrance to the Aokigahara Jukai 'sea of trees' forest, and is regarded as one of the tourist spots within the Fuji Five Lakes area that can be visited throughout the year. Over 1150 years ago, during year 6 of the Jogan era (864 a.d.), Nagaoyama, a flank volcano of Mt. Fuji erupted. The red hot lava flow (Aokigahara Maruo) descended between ancient parasitic volcanoes, creating this two-tunnel type cave. After being designated by the Ministry of Education as a natural monument in 1929, it was introduced to the world as a geological wonder. By the way, the tree-type lava bed is said to have the most spiracles in the world. Since the cave is situated in a ring-like manner, visitors can view its various features by making one circular loop. The average temperature inside the cave is 3degC, that's why it is called an Ice Cave. The total length of the cave is 150m and requires 6-7 mins to have a complete view inside the cave.

title: Fuji Safari Park | 富士サファリパーク
description:
At the foot of Mt. Fuji lies this enormous animal park. Divided into 2 major zones, the Safari Zone and Fureai Zone.

Safari Zone is a 50min drive through where you can find 7 zones of different animals from all over the world. Riding on your own car, you cannot open your windows or doors as it could be too dangerous. But there is an option of riding the Jungle Bus where you can feed the animals yourself. these huge animals come to the jungle bus seeking for food, as close as 20cm apart from you, with just steel mesh in between. You can also opt to try their 4WD vehicle and experience the same as the jungle bus, feed the animals as they come near you and wait to be fed.

The fureai zone on the other hand is extremely different as you can have a friendly contact with the animals. you can feed them upclose, hold them in your arms and caress them as long as you want. Great for kids and animal lovers.

For more information, visit their website:
https://www.fujisafari.co.jp/en/
